questions.q: What four core Azure resources does this Terraform configuration provision?
options: An S3 bucket, an IAM role, an EC2 instance, and a VPC
A resource group, a virtual network with a subnet, an Azure Container Registry, and an AKS cluster
A single Azure VM and a Blob Storage container
A Terraform Cloud workspace and nothing else
questions.explain: The configuration provisions rg-driftwood-prod, a VNet/subnet, acrdriftwoodprod, and the aks-driftwood-prod cluster.

questions.q: What does the `helm_release` Terraform resource do in this configuration?
options: It deletes the AKS cluster
It installs the storefront app's Helm chart onto the cluster as part of the same `terraform apply`
It only validates YAML syntax without deploying anything
It creates the AWS S3 backup bucket
questions.explain: `helm_release` lets `terraform apply` provision the cluster and install the app's chart in one pass.

questions.q: Where did the `minReplicas: 10` value in `values-prod.yaml` actually come from?
options: Theo calculated it from Driftwood's historical traffic data
A values-prod.yaml template reused from a former colleague's much higher-traffic retail client engagement
AKS's default value for every cluster
Casey specifically requested exactly 10 replicas
questions.explain: Theo adapted a known-good template from a previous, busier engagement as a reasonable starting point under deadline pressure.

questions.q: What does `minReplicas: 10` actually guarantee, regardless of how much real traffic the app sees?
options: That the app will never go down
That at least 10 pods run at all times, even during periods of very low traffic
That the cluster will automatically scale down to zero overnight
That exactly 10 customers can use the app simultaneously
questions.explain: minReplicas sets a floor: the autoscaler keeps at least that many pods running at all times, independent of actual demand.

questions.q: Why doesn't Theo immediately flag `minReplicas: 10` as a mistake at the end of this lesson?
options: Because it clearly is not a mistake and never will be
Because it's a valid, well-formed value reused from a battle-tested template, and right-sizing it was a mental note that didn't make it onto a ticket
Because Terraform would refuse to apply an incorrect value
Because Priya explicitly approved exactly this number
questions.explain: The value looks like responsible reuse of proven configuration, not an obvious error — the kind of decision that's easy to lose track of under deadline pressure.
